magnitude_lanes.match_title: Unstructured youth recreation centre participation and antisocial behaviour development: Selection influences and the moderating role of antisocial peers
magnitude_lanes.authors: Joseph L. Mahoney, Håkan Stattin, Heather Lord

the_zero_skatepark_crime_literature_clau: The founder's spec asked for skate-park CRIME outcomes: the peer-reviewed literature has essentially NO direct crime-outcome studies of skate parks. What exists is 3 lanes: (a) the flagship triad (Skate Parks as a Context for Adolescent Development, 34c) — users show NORMAL adjustment/integration, zero deviance deficit; (b) the design/injury lane — skatepark injuries patterned by park design; (c) the physical-activity lane — sessions meet CDC heart-rate targets. The crime question is literally unanswered — the honest-null is the scan's headline for this band.
the_pool_block_warning_clause: The aquatic band carries an unexpected NEGATIVE: the highest-cited youth-center outcome in the whole scan (Unstructured youth recreation centre participation, 95c, N=1,163, 2-y longitudinal) finds unstructured drop-in center participation INCREASES antisocial behaviour after selection controls — peer aggregation without structure. Any municipal unstructured youth-space spend (pool open-swim, rec center drop-in) needs programming structure to avoid the Örebro result.
the_facility_proximity_clause: Colleges and Community Crime (19c): infrastructure that congregates youth raises NEARBY crime through opportunity/routine-activity. The closest analog to pool/library crime-outcome questions — and it cuts against the naive 'build it and crime falls' prior. Libraries have NO direct crime-outcome literature; their lane runs through summer-reading achievement (the 2012 multi-site positive, qualified by the 2011 Overstating reanalysis) and the social-infrastructure framing (Klinenberg).
the_sports_nul_l_clause: The biggest-N finding in the scan: sports participation ∄ delinquency at N=132,366 (431 ES, 48 samples) ≈ zero aggregate. Recreation does not reduce crime through participation per se; the After-School meta (17 studies) gives the small-but-positive structured-programming read. The strata law repeats: STRUCTURE carries the effect, unstructured access does not.
the_capital_rct_clause: Where the causal evidence is actually strong: municipal LOT/STRUCTURE remediation. Philadelphia cluster-RCTs (2013 Inj Prev, 2019 AJPH citywide, 2026 PNAS 10-y), abandoned-housing RCT (JAMA IM 2023), New Orleans family-violence RCT (2026). Direction consistent, BUT heterogeneous: gains concentrate in mid-disadvantaged neighborhoods and are NULL in the poorest — the spending-targeting law. Collective efficacy (9,003c) is the mediating variable every lane routes through.
the_midnight_basketball_surprise_clause: Rethinking Sports-Based Community Crime Prevention (63c): early-adopter midnight-basketball cities showed sharper property-crime decreases — the mocked 1994 Crime Bill program gets a (confounded) quasi-confirmation. Sports/recreation effects on crime likely run through diffuse indirect mechanisms, not hours-on-court.
